knowledge_point.title: Constructing Line Integrals With Respect to X

question.:question/problem:
![Oriented path](/tmp/ca9837-templates-z7ii9jxi/17592186133891/path-6732a9233b2a88097084e1af.png)

Which definite integral is equivalent to

$$
\int_C x y^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

where $C$ is the line segment traversed from $(1,3)$ to $(-3,5)$, as shown? Do not evaluate the integral.

*Hint: Use $\mathbf r(t)=\langle 1 - 4 t,2 t + 3\rangle$.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Interpolate from the initial point to the terminal point. The parameter starts at $0$ and ends at $1$, giving the required endpoints.

$$
\mathbf r(t)=\langle 1 - 4 t,2 t + 3\rangle,\qquad 0\le t\le 1
$$

Substitute both coordinates, then differentiate the first coordinate:

$$
\begin{aligned} f(\mathbf r(t))&=(1 - 4 t)(2 t + 3)^{2}\\&=- 16 t^{3} - 44 t^{2} - 24 t + 9,\\ x\prime(t)&=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the two factors, keeping the signed derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(t))x\prime(t)&=(- 16 t^{3} - 44 t^{2} - 24 t + 9)(-4)\\&=64 t^{3} + 176 t^{2} + 96 t - 36.\end{aligned}
$$

Use this density with the oriented parameter limits:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C x y^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x&=\int_{0}^{1} f(\mathbf r(t))x\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\\&=\int_{0}^{1} 64 t^{3} + 176 t^{2} + 96 t - 36\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

derivation_conversions: distribute products and collect like factors

question.:question/problem:
![Oriented path](/tmp/ca9837-templates-z7ii9jxi/17592186133891/path-4bbb2298ca48f7c33bf715f9.png)

Which definite integral is equivalent to

$$
\int_C x y^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

where $C$ is the arc of $16 x^{2} + y^{2}=16$, traversed counterclockwise through three quarters of the ellipse from $(\frac{1}{2},2 \sqrt{3})$ to $(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},-2)$, as shown? Do not evaluate the integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The coordinate scales follow from $\frac{x^2}{1}+\frac{y^2}{16}=1$. Choose the parametrization below. Increasing the parameter follows the stated counterclockwise direction. At the initial endpoint, $\cos t=\frac{x}{1}=\frac{1}{2}$ and $\sin t=\frac{y}{4}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. Thus the initial parameter in $[0,2\pi)$ is $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Continue the parameter through $\frac{3 \pi}{2}$ to follow the stated arc. The parameter starts at $\frac{\pi}{3}$ and ends at $\frac{11 \pi}{6}$, giving the required endpoints.

$$
\mathbf r(t)=\langle \cos{\left(t \right)},4 \sin{\left(t \right)}\rangle,\qquad \frac{\pi}{3}\le t\le \frac{11 \pi}{6}
$$

Substitute both coordinates, then differentiate the first coordinate:

$$
\begin{aligned} f(\mathbf r(t))&=(\cos{\left(t \right)})(4 \sin{\left(t \right)})^{2}\\&=16 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)},\\ x\prime(t)&=- \sin{\left(t \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the two factors, keeping the signed derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(t))x\prime(t)&=(16 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)})(- \sin{\left(t \right)})\\&=- 16 \sin^{3}{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Use this density with the oriented parameter limits:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C x y^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x&=\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{11 \pi}{6}} f(\mathbf r(t))x\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\\&=\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{11 \pi}{6}} - 16 \sin^{3}{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
